quotes.text: Keep in mind that you continue to be responsible for any disputes opened before the migration.
Tell your customers that no further action is required from them, unless they choose to cancel the mandate.
Inform your customers after you successfully process the first payment post-migration.
You can also retrieve it by [listing](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/list.md) all PaymentMethods for the customer.

old_evidence.text: Stripe might require you to provide copies of the Authorities, and you must do so promptly.
You must send this notification in addition to the automatic notification that Stripe sends after successfully importing your customer bank account details.
If you’ve turned off automatic notifications by Stripe, you must notify your customers.

findings: The stable flow starts with proof of an existing mandate from each customer and preserves pre-migration dispute responsibility. The guide says to notify customers before migration, state no action is required unless canceling, then send a distinct notice after the first successful pay-in. Stripe's default notices are after successful import and on each later debit, with substitute merchant notices when disabled (old raw lines 8-30 and new raw lines 9-31).

The two server paths create or find the related customer-configured Account or Customer then attempt to confirm one SetupIntent per customer and bank account. The request uses `payment_method_data[type]=nz_bank_account`, bank/branch/account/suffix, customer name and email, and offline mandate acceptance with the original authorization date. The shown epoch is illustrative. The final step stores or retrieves the PaymentMethod ID for future payment use (old raw lines 34-103 and new raw lines 33-76).

The only November body differences are Node to curl, equivalent representation of nested parameters, step numbering and heading whitespace. Both retain both identity paths, authorization timing and required customer notifications (diff lines 3-108). No new API/SDK requirement, UI rollout or scope change follows from the example language.

Wiki index line 7 routes to Stripe index lines 259-262 and 742. NZ BECS concept lines 22-42 and 82-85 provides the reciprocal route. Qualify the source and the concept route so the linked overview's general deadline is distinct from the migration-specific notice split.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the May 3, 2026 capture and historical Node examples (old raw lines 2 and 39-103) alongside dated November curl. Keep the original DDA timestamp scope, two alternative customer identities, required name and email, and three notice classes with their distinct events.

Neither capture changes the rule for disputes opened before migration, DDA copy retention and prompt request response, the original date of authorization, or the customer cancellation boundary (old raw lines 8-37 and new raw lines 9-38).
conflicts: Current source lines 13 and 17-24 omit two independent obligations explicitly present in both captures. Retain each original DDA, provide requested copies to Stripe promptly, and remain responsible for disputes opened before migration. If Stripe automatic notices have been disabled, the merchant must provide the applicable mandate confirmation and per-debit notifications. The separate merchant first-debit notice is sent after the first successful post-migration payment and is additional to Stripe's successful-import confirmation. Merchant pre-migration notice comes before transfer, includes Stripe New Zealand Limited, code 3143978, the transfer date and merchant support details, and tells the customer no further action is required unless they cancel (old raw lines 8-30 and new raw lines 9-31).

Correct both reciprocal references, wiki/concepts/stripe-nz-becs-debit.md:36 and wiki/sources/source-stripe-nz-becs-debit.md:25. They currently state that the mandatory pre-debit notice is due on the day of PaymentIntent confirmation. The May overview sets the obligation on debit day (old overview lines 135-161). The November overview sets it no later than debit day (new overview lines 224-249). Both separately describe the default per-debit email as sent immediately after a successful PaymentIntent confirmation. The merchant should contact Stripe Support to turn off those automatic emails and send its own replacements, as November overview line 228 documents and May overview line 139 also states. Source lines 21-24 and concept line 85 should keep the successful-import mandate confirmation, each debit notice, and the merchant's separate notice after the first successful post-migration payment distinct (old raw lines 20-30 and new raw lines 21-31). The original DDA accepted_at remains the historical authorization time.

Current source lines 26-32 should spell out that customer_account selects a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account, while customer selects a Customers v1 Customer, as alternatives associated with the migrated bank account. They are different from the NZ bank account itself, the DDA, the SetupIntent and the resulting PaymentMethod. Save or retrieve the PaymentMethod ID, and retain the documentary authorization separately (old raw lines 34-69 and 71-103; new raw lines 33-76). The separate November SetupIntent Create reference lines 370-386 describes confirm=true as an attempt and attaches the method only on successful setup. The SetupIntent object's payment_method is nullable and status lifecycle appears at its lines 591-614. A successful import establishes setup, without proving any first debit, payment success, funds availability or permission to ignore a canceled mandate.

Old and new migration captures link to future use but do not promise off-session payment execution. The November NZ BECS API matrix marks off-session payments unsupported at overview lines 191-208. Separate November acceptance and save-for-future pages show later server PaymentIntents with off_session=true after attachment (acceptance lines 291-320 and setup lines 259-296). Preserve the dated conflict on the related acceptance/setup/overview routes and qualify any migration bridge. Successful migration, method attachment, and mandate status are distinct from later request success, payment confirmation or settlement.
unresolved_questions: The migration captures do not specify an exact schedule for merchant notification beyond before transfer and after first successful debit, how to transfer a dispute opened earlier, or account-specific access for any customer-configured Account. They also do not resolve the separate overview/acceptance off-session conflict.

source_assessments.reason: The raw comparison is semantically stable. The baseline still omits notification fallback, prior-dispute ownership and timely DDA copy production and leaves the first-debit trigger compressed.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account/migrate-from-another-processor documents importing an already authorized NZ BECS bank account. Retain each original Direct Debit Authority, promptly give Stripe copies when requested, and remain responsible for disputes opened before migration. Before transfer, tell customers the processor is Stripe New Zealand Limited, code 3143978, give the date Stripe begins processing and merchant support details, and explain that customers need only act if they want to cancel. Send a separate merchant notice after the first successful post-migration payment. Stripe normally sends a mandate notice after successful import and a pre-debit notice for each later payment. If automatic Stripe notices are off, the merchant must send the applicable replacements (new raw lines 9-31). For each customer and bank account, create or find either a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account using customer_account or a Customers v1 Customer using customer. Attempt to confirm a SetupIntent with nz_bank_account bank, branch, account and suffix values, required billing name and email, and offline mandate acceptance using the original authorization timestamp. Retrieve and store the PaymentMethod ID from the response or by listing the customer's methods (new raw lines 33-76). Setup and successful import are distinct from confirming or settling a later debit. The May 3 capture documents the same requirements and both identity paths in Node (old raw lines 8-37 and 39-103). source-stripe-nz-becs-migrate-from-processor.md summarizes the steps but omits prompt copy production, earlier dispute responsibility, and the seller notice fallback, and should make the first-success trigger explicit.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account/migrate-from-another-processor the November change is presentational. cURL replaces Node, preserves both customer identity routes, the underlying request fields, and original offline mandate acceptance, with renumbering and whitespace changes (old raw lines 32-103 and new raw lines 33-76). The captures do not establish a substantive migration behavior or API-version change. Preserve May 3 evidence in source-stripe-nz-becs-migrate-from-processor.md and correct its omissions independently. The early customer notice, successful-import mandate email, per-payment debit notification and merchant notice after first successful payment remain distinct, including the mandate and debit notices the seller supplies when Stripe automation is disabled. The seller must promptly supply retained original DDAs if requested, and disputes opened before migration remain with the seller (old raw lines 8-30 and new raw lines 9-31). Correct wiki/concepts/stripe-nz-becs-debit.md:36 and wiki/sources/source-stripe-nz-becs-debit.md:25, which currently use PaymentIntent confirmation day as the mandatory deadline. The May NZ BECS overview places the obligation on debit day (old overview lines 135-161). The November NZ BECS overview says no later than debit day (new overview lines 224-249). Both describe Stripe’s default immediate send after successful PaymentIntent confirmation as a separate trigger. To turn off the default emails and send replacements, the merchant contacts Stripe Support (November overview line 228 and May overview line 139). Successful-import confirmation and each pre-debit notice remain distinct from the merchant's additional notice after the first successful post-migration payment. The original accepted_at timestamp records the historical authorization. Both server examples attempt SetupIntent confirmation for a customer-configured Account or Customer. Save the resulting PaymentMethod ID after successful setup without inferring a successful debit, settlement or broader eligibility. The November overview's off-session exclusion and separate November acceptance/setup examples for a later off_session=true PaymentIntent remain unresolved for that separate payment flow. The migration guide links to future payments and gives no off-session outcome (old raw lines 94-103 and new raw lines 61-76).
